# Temple Scroll Column 61 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 61 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**61:1** When you go out to war against your enemies, and I, the LORD your God, deliver them into your hand, and you take captives from among them,

**61:2** and you see among the captives a woman of beautiful appearance, and you desire her and wish to take her as your wife,

**61:3** you shall bring her into your house, and she shall shave her head and trim her nails.

**61:4** She shall remove the garment of her captivity from upon her and shall dwell in your house, weeping for her father and her mother for a full month.

**61:5** After that you may go in to her and be her husband, and she shall become your wife.

**61:6** And if it comes to pass that you do not delight in her, you shall let her go wherever she desires; but you shall by no means sell her for money.

**61:7** You shall not treat her as a slave, because you have humbled her.

**61:8** If a man has two wives, one loved and the other unloved, and both the loved and the unloved bear him sons,

**61:9** and the firstborn son is the son of the unloved wife, then on the day he bequeaths his possessions to his sons,

**61:10** he may not treat the son of the loved wife as the firstborn in preference to the son of the unloved wife, who is in fact the firstborn.

**61:11** Rather, he shall acknowledge the firstborn, the son of the unloved wife, by giving him a double share of all that he possesses,

**61:12** for that son is the first fruit of his vigor; the right of the firstborn belongs to him.

**61:13** If a man has a stubborn and rebellious son who will not obey the voice of his father or the voice of his mother,

**61:14** and although they discipline him he will not listen to them, then his father and his mother shall take hold of him and bring him out to the elders of his city, at the gate of his place.

**61:15** They shall say to the elders of his city: This son of ours is stubborn and rebellious; he will not obey us; he is a glutton and a drunkard.

**61:16** Then all the men of his city shall stone him to death with stones. So you shall purge the evil from your midst, and all Israel shall hear and be afraid.

---

*LOGOS notes: Column 61 reworks Deut 21:10–21 into divine first-person address. "Deliver" for נתן in military context; "treat her as a slave" for תתעמר clarifies the sense for English readers. "Unloved" preferred over "hated" as formal equivalent for שנואה in marital context. "First fruit of his vigor" renders ראשית אונו with dignified register.*
